idea: Build QuickBite, a student meal planner app with dorm recipes and cooking timers
problem: College students living in dorms often lack proper kitchen appliances, cooking experience, time, and budget, leading to unhealthy eating habits and overspending on food delivery.
targetUsers: University students living in residence halls with restricted cooking setups
First-time independent young adults on strict budgets with limited kitchen skills
valueProposition: A hyper-localized meal planning and recipe app specifically designed for micro-kitchens and dorm appliances (microwaves, mug meals, air fryers) featuring budget tracking and integrated cooking timers.
competitionAssessment: General meal planning apps (Mealime, Yummly, Tasty) and budget recipe blogs (Budget Bytes) exist, but none exclusively focus on low-equipment, dorm-safe constraint filtering alongside native interactive timers.
differentiation: Strict appliance-based filtering (e.g., microwave-only, kettle-only), automatic grocery budget capping per recipe, and built-in multi-timer flows tailored for quick dorm prep.
technicalFeasibility: High feasibility. Standard mobile app architecture (React Native/Flutter) with straightforward database requirements for recipes, local notification APIs for timers, and low infrastructure costs.
monetizationPotential: Moderate to low directly from users due to high price sensitivity of students. Best monetized via freemium tiers, grocery delivery affiliate links (Instacart/Walmart), and targeted brand sponsorships.
keyRisks: Low willingness to pay among the target college demographic
High user churn as students graduate or move into full apartments
Strong competition from free visual cooking content on TikTok and YouTube
